newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Soros buys in as Venezuela Sudamtex turns to oil.
newsitem.headline: Soros buys in as Venezuela Sudamtex turns to oil.

text.p: George Soros' recent purchase of a 24 percent stake in Venezuelan-based multinational Sudamtex reflects a change in company focus towards the oil sector and away from textiles, company officials said.
"You have to recognize that Venezuela is every day more an oil country," executive vice president Luis Antonio Sotillo told reporters.

Sotillo said the 50-year old company, which has traditionally focused on textiles and synthetic fabrics, would invest $70 million over the next four years in its expanding fiber-glass business throughout Latin America, used to make storage tanks and high pressure tubing for the oil sector.
The company signed a contract with state-owned oil company PdVSA in April 1996 to provide double-skinned storage tanks.

"We're still thinking about the best way to finance that (investment), maybe debt, maybe a share offer, or a mixture of both. Either way, we're consulting with Soros who clearly has a lot of experience there," he said.

New York-based financial guru George Soros's Quantum Fund increased its stake in the company last Friday to 24 percent when it bought 3.45 million American Depository Receipts in the secondary market after talks with the company.
"We're the only fiber-glass company in the Andean pact," said Sotillo, adding that third quarter company results due next Wednesday "will hold no surprises."

Sudamtex reported first half profits of 6.3 billion bolivars on 33.7 billion bolivars of sales compared to 5.1 billion bolivars on 38.7 billion bolivars of sales over the same period in the year before.
